chapter: Eddie Heywood, the organ and later work
title: Heywood records the first "Lover Man" on Commodore
summary: Heywood made the first instrumental "Lover Man" on the back of "Begin the Beguine" and outsold Billie.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: What do you call... He used to work for Decca....
He had a record store. Remember when they had 12-inch records?
So Eddie made the first record of 'Lover Man' that was made. Instrumental. There was no voice. That hadn't come into the picture yet.
Was that on the back of 'Begin The Beguine'?
The Commodore label. He did that. And he made a solo out of 'Lover Man.'
On the back of 'Begin the Beguine'?
Yeah, on the back of it.
So in a way, that established 'Lover Man' for you.
Exactly. That's right. And he outsold Billie Holiday. And they were the ten-inchers; a ten-inch record that had 'Lover Man' on the other side as an instrumental.
So you had like a double shot at that.
Yeah. And so 'Begin The Beguine,' naturally it was good for 'Lover Man.'
